description: Evolution ladder v2 (live since 2026-10-29): Knuckle-Dragger, Primate, Neanderthal, Prime, Silverback, Kong, Apex. Stage bars follow Strength Level population percentiles at the lifter's sex and bodyweight (curve), rounded to 5 lb / 2.5 kg as shown (rounding). A strength game ladder: a model, not a measurement. Strength alone earns every rank. Generated by tools/build_evolution.py; do not hand-edit.
rank_id: language-neutral "<stage_id>.<tier>" (e.g. "primate.2"); index = 3 x stage index + tier - 1 (0..20). Only display labels carry names. Stage ids are unchanged from ladder v1; only prime and silverback swap positions (prime: stage 4 -> 3, silverback: 3 -> 4), so their rank indexes change (prime.N 12-14 -> 9-11, silverback.N 9-11 -> 12-14).
rank_threshold_rule: bars at bodyweight BW: stage entries from curve (percentiles on SL's tiers at BW); tier 1 = stage entry; Chief = entry + 1/3 x (next entry - entry); Alpha = + 2/3; the Apex gap runs to the 99th-percentile ceiling. Then rounding (nearest 5 lb / 2.5 kg for loads with the monotonic guard; whole reps, rounded up, for pull-ups and dips).

table_choice.unset_label: Using the men's table. Set sex in Settings to use the women's table.

value.reps: best-ever strict-rep value. A set with no added load counts its reps (any rep count). A weighted set (added load > 0, reps 1..12) converts to strict-rep equivalents [M]: E = (f x BW + added) x (1 + reps/30) is its estimated 1RM, and the strict reps that reach the same estimate at bodyweight alone are r_eq = 30 x (E / (f x BW) - 1), floored to a whole rep. f = exercises.json bodyweight_fraction (0.95), BW = bodyweight on the set's day (a weighted set without a bodyweight is not rated). Negative logged loads (assistance) are not counted. Same deload / tag exclusions (tags with reps_at_load in pr_exclude excluded for strict sets, e1rm for weighted sets). Compared with the whole-rep bars at the set's day bodyweight (a strict set with no bodyweight on file uses the anchor bodyweight bars: 180 lb men, 145 lb women).
value.weighted_conversion_note: A model: Epley extrapolated to high reps is rough, so converted values are approximate. Labelled "Includes weighted sets (converted to strict reps, estimated)."
value.load: best-ever estimated 1RM (Epley load x (1 + reps/30), working sets with 1..12 reps, deload sessions and pr_exclude e1rm tags excluded), compared with the bars as shown at the set's day bodyweight in the display unit; best-ever = the set with the highest ladder position (rounding.position). report().lifts.<lift>.value = that estimated 1RM in the display unit; multiple = estimated 1RM / bodyweight (display only).

bodyweight.rule: bodyweight for a set = the latest history.bodyweights entry dated on or before the set's session local date (startedAt || date); none -> settings.profile.bodyweight; none -> load lifts (and weighted rep sets) are not rated; strict reps use the anchor bodyweight bars.
bodyweight.current: for next-rank targets: latest entry on or before as_of; none -> settings.profile.bodyweight; none -> no load targets (rep targets at the anchor bodyweight).
bodyweight.note: Unlike prs.py there is no backfill from a later entry: a later weigh-in never rewrites an older rank.

promotion.rule: overall rank = the highest rank index met by at least 3 of the 5 core lifts (after at most one stand-in substitution). A lift meets a rank when its best ladder position >= that rank's index, i.e. its estimated 1RM (or reps) reached the bar as shown at that set's bodyweight. Unlogged or unrated lifts meet nothing. Everyone starts at knuckle_dragger.1.
promotion.never_demote: shown rank = max(computed rank, history.evolution.awarded). The app stores the highest rank shown in history.evolution.awarded {stage, tier, ladder_version: 2}; a drop, a bodyweight gain, a sex change or a deleted set never lowers it (held: true while computed < awarded).
promotion.per_lift_stage: each lift (core and stand-ins) shows its own rank: the highest rank whose threshold it meets (hidden stages beyond the revealed ladder show as "Locked stage").

stand_ins.scale: barbell row estimated 1RM vs curve.tables.<sex>.row (SL bent-over row percentiles)
stand_ins.source: Strength Level bent-over row standards by bodyweight (men and women)

stand_ins.scale: strict dip reps vs curve.tables.<sex>.dips (SL dips percentiles)
stand_ins.source: Strength Level dips standards by bodyweight (men and women)

substitution.rule: only when a core lift is not trained (no qualifying working set ever, deload excluded) and its stand-in has a rated value. At most one substitution; if two are possible, take the one giving the higher overall rank, then higher overall progress, then the order above. A trained-but-unrated core lift (e.g. no bodyweight) is not substituted.
substitution.label: {stand_in} stands in for {lift}

progress.per_lift: p = clamp(position - s, 0, 1), with position the lift's best ladder position (rounding.position) and s the shown overall rank; unlogged / unrated -> 0.
progress.overall: 3rd-highest of the 5 slot progresses (core lifts after substitution). It reaches 1.0 exactly when a 3rd lift meets the next rank, which is the promotion rule. At the top rank (apex.3) progress is null.

targets.rule: for each slot: the next rank's bar as shown at the current bodyweight in the display unit (load lifts: an estimated 1RM on the 5 lb / 2.5 kg grid; rep lifts: whole reps). Reaching exactly that number earns the rank on that lift. No current bodyweight -> no load target (reps use the anchor bodyweight).

hidden.rule: kong and apex stages (only these two; silverback is visible) show as "Locked stage" in the ladder, the next-rank name and per-lift stages until the overall rank (with the awarded floor) reaches them.
hidden.label: Locked stage

plate_badges.unit_setting: settings.unit ("lb" default | "kg") picks the set; both lists exist
plate_badges.rule: earned by the first done working set (non-deload, reps >= 1, not tagged with weight in pr_exclude) whose logged load, converted to the setting unit, is >= the plate load - 0.01. A real set, not an estimate. Independent of rank.
plate_badges.hidden_rule: The five-plate badges (495 lb / 220 kg: five 45 lb or 20 kg plates a side on a 45 lb / 20 kg bar) on bench, squat and deadlift are hidden until earned. Only these entries carry a hidden key: hidden: true and label "Hidden badge" until a qualifying set exists, then hidden: false and the normal label, shown like the other plate badges. Plates 1-4 have no hidden key. Overhead press stays at two plates. Not a tier; independent of rank.
plate_badges.decision: Five plates on all three barbell lifts, all hidden until earned: one simple rule for the top plate. A 495 lb bench is the rare one (above the Apex bench at 180 lb); for a 180 lb man a 495 squat comes between Silverback (474) and Kong (529) and a 495 deadlift just before Silverback (513), so they act as a surprise along the way rather than an end-game marker.

lean.purpose: Opt-in physique condition that unlocks ONLY the "Lean Prime" art and badge. It never affects rank. A leanness game condition, not a health measure.

badge.label: Lean Prime
badge.rule: unlocked when lean.status == pass and the shown rank is at stage prime or above; stale -> shown greyed (prime is stage 3 in ladder v2, so silverback, kong and apex also qualify)

lean.opt_in: settings.bodyComp.optIn === true. Never on by default; never asked during onboarding.
lean.hide_switch: settings.bodyComp.hidden === true hides every body-composition field, status and badge (status "hidden").
lean.under_18: settings.profile.birthDate (YYYY-MM-DD) gives age at as_of; under 18 -> no body-composition features at all (status "unavailable"). Age unknown -> not offered until a birth date is entered (status "needs_age" when opted in).
lean.inputs: settings.profile.height {value, unit:"cm"|"in"}; history.bodyComp [{date, waist?:{value, unit}, bfPct?, bfMethod?:"dexa"|"calipers"|"bia"|"eye"}]

primary.label: Waist-to-height ratio
primary.measure: waist at the navel, standing relaxed, after a normal breath out, divided by height (same units)

fallback.label: Entered body-fat %
fallback.used_when: no waist entry (with a height) in the window
fallback.note: Body-fat readings can be off by 3-5 points.

lean.reading_rule: use the best (lowest) reading of the decisive method dated within the last 90 days up to as_of, so the mark does not flicker; only older readings -> stale (greyed).
lean.sex_rule: same as the strength table: unset -> men's thresholds, with the same label
lean.copy_rules: Use "lean" and "visible physique". Never "healthy", "fit" or "ideal"; no "lose X" prompts; no streaks, notifications or comparisons tied to waist or weight.

labels.needs_entry: Add a waist or body-fat entry to track your physique
labels.needs_age: Add your birth date to use physique tracking
labels.stale: Update your waist to keep the Lean mark

ladder_hidden.rule: settings.ladder.hidden === true hides the whole ladder UI (rank chip, ladder, progress bar, next-rank targets, plate badges, Lean Prime). Display flag only: report() output is identical either way, ranks keep being computed, history.evolution.awarded keeps updating, and nothing is ever demoted or reset. Turning it off shows the current rank.
ladder_hidden.separate_from: settings.bodyComp.hidden (hides only body-composition fields, status and the Lean Prime badge). The two flags are independent; either can be on.

data_schema.history.evolution: {awarded?: {stage, tier, ladder_version?: 2}} - written by the app after showing a rank (report().awarded_out); never lowered. No ladder_version (or 1) = ladder v1 order, migrated on read (migration).
data_schema.note: all optional; include in backup / restore

labels.source_note: Stages follow Strength Level percentiles: the share of Strength Level users (self-logged lifts) a bar beats at your sex and bodyweight. Strength Level is not peer-reviewed, and some ranges are estimated from other published standards. The percentile line is an estimate. Estimated 1RM is a model, not a measured max.
labels.ladder_hidden_note: Ladder hidden. Your rank is still tracked and is never lowered.
labels.model_note: Ranks are a strength game based on a model, not a measurement of health or fitness.
labels.promotion_note: Promotion needs 3 of 5 core lifts. Ranks are never taken away.
labels.held_note: Rank kept: ranks are never taken away.
labels.weighted_note: Includes weighted sets (converted to strict reps, estimated).
labels.bars_note: Bars follow Strength Level standards for your sex and bodyweight.
labels.percentile_line: Stronger than about {pct}% of lifters your size

migration.detect: history.evolution.awarded without ladder_version (or ladder_version 1) is a v1 award. Accepted v1 forms: {stage, tier} (stage id + tier, the documented form), {index} or a bare integer (a v1 rank index 0..20).
migration.rule: For a stored v1 award at v1 index i (0..20; old stage order, old flat tables for the user's current sex table), at this lifter's current bodyweight (no bodyweight -> the anchor bodyweight, 180 lb men, 145 lb women): (1) t = 3 of 5: the HIGHEST v2 rank where at least 3 of the 5 core slots have a v2 bar <= the v1 rank's bar for that lift x (1 + tolerance) (load lifts: the v2 curve bar, unrounded lb, vs the v1 multiple x bodyweight x 1.03; pull-ups and dips: the whole-rep v2 bar vs the v1 reps x 1.03); a failing core slot may count through its stand-in (barbell row for pull-ups, dips for bench press) when the stand-in passes, at most one substitution. (2) p = i: the same step number on the v2 ladder. (3) q = the previous floor: the HIGHEST v2 rank whose bars on all 5 core lifts are each <= the v1 bars x (1 + tolerance). (4) floor = max(t, p, q). (5) Hidden cap: a migration never unlocks a hidden stage on its own: if floor >= the first Kong index (15) and t < 15, the floor is capped at Alpha Silverback (14); likewise, if floor >= the first Apex index (18) and t < 18, it is capped at Alpha Kong (17). Only a real 3-of-5 result can place a migrated award in Kong or Apex. tolerance = 0.03. All of this applies ONLY to migrating a stored v1 award; computed ranks never use it. Then shown = max(computed v2 rank, floor); awarded_out is written back with ladder_version 2 and never lowered again.
migration.why_not_by_id: ids are stable but silverback moved above prime: copying "silverback.2" across would promote a v1 Chief Silverback (bench 1.08x) past Prime (1.25x). Copying the index would rename ranks arbitrarily.
migration.labels_note: The floor is at least the same step number as the v1 award (a v1 Prime, step 12, lands at least at Silverback, step 12, in v2) and never below the previous floor, except that a migration alone never reaches Kong or Apex; see migration.table. The computed rank from the user's logged lifts can land higher; nothing the user lifted is lost.
migration.output: report().awarded_migration = {from: v1 id, from_index, to: v2 id, to_index} when a v1 award was read, else null.
migration.table_note: migration.table is computed at the anchor bodyweight (180 lb men, 145 lb women) with the 3% tolerance: three_of_five_index = t, same_step_index = p, previous_floor_index = q, hidden_cap = true when step (5) lowered the floor (to Alpha Silverback or Alpha Kong); no_tolerance_floor_index = the full rule without the tolerance. The app computes the floor at the lifter's current bodyweight.

progression_model.text: Estimated 1RM grows by a fixed weekly percentage that falls with training age: 2.5% in weeks 1-12, 1.5% in weeks 13-26, 0.9% to the end of year 1, 0.5% in year 2, 0.25% in years 3-4, 0.12% in years 5-8 and 0.06% from year 9 (the last step models diminishing returns). Constant bodyweight, each lift trained 1-2x a week. Start multiples = a first-month beginner (men bench 0.40, squat 0.50, deadlift 0.60, OHP 0.25; women = the men's start x the women/men Prime ratio, so both reach Prime at the same model age). Knuckle-Dragger entry = the start (curve.tables.<sex>.<lift>.kd_fraction). Model months use the bars as shown at the anchor bodyweight. Stage years = the 3rd-fastest of the four barbell lifts (3 of 5 lifts promote; pull-ups assumed to keep pace). A smooth curve chosen to resemble typical progress: an estimate, not a study result; real progress varies widely.

table_units: tables.<sex>.<lift> is DOCUMENTATION at the anchor bodyweight (men 180 lb, women 145 lb): raw stage entries and bars in lb (reps for pull-ups / dips) and the bars as shown in lb. The app computes bars at every bodyweight from curve (curve.tables.<sex>.<lift>.rows) and rounding; do not read ranks from this block.

standards.note: Every bar below was read from the cited public page on the access date. None of these sources is peer-reviewed. Loads in lb at the anchor bodyweight (men 180 lb, women 145 lb); kg tables converted at 2.20462 lb/kg. Cross-reference only since the Strength Level percentile ladder: stage bars come from curve.

uspa.name: USPA classification standards (Classic Raw, Open)
uspa.basis: Official USPA classification calculator data (Class IV to International Elite) for competition 1RMs. Men 82.5 kg class, women 67.5 kg class; Classic Raw = knee sleeves (closest to OpenPowerlifting "Raw"). The old uspa.net/classification-standards.html address now redirects to the calculator.

fpr.name: Russian Powerlifting Federation (FPR) sport-rank standards, classic bench press
fpr.basis: Unified All-Russian Sports Classification (Minsport order No. 299 of 09.04.2026, valid 09.06.2026-31.12.2029). Classic (raw) bench-press discipline, men 83 kg and women 69 kg classes: 3rd / 2nd / 1st adult rank, CMS, MS. Women's table read from the St Petersburg federation mirror (men's rows match the official page). FPR publishes raw squat and deadlift only as part of the full-power total, so it is used for bench only.

strength_level.name: Strength Level
strength_level.basis: Self-logged lifts of its users. Men: 180 lb row; women: midpoint of the 140 and 150 lb rows.

symmetric_strength.name: Symmetric Strength
symmetric_strength.basis: Model bands. Men: published 180 lb example; women: published 140 lb example (145 lb needs the JavaScript calculator; bars a few % higher).

exrx.name: ExRx.net weightlifting performance standards
exrx.basis: Classification-style tables. Men 181 lb class, women 148 lb class.

openpowerlifting.name: OpenPowerlifting
openpowerlifting.basis: Public-domain competition results (data date 2026-10-24); percentiles computed here (see opl).

standards.checked_not_used: IPF and USAPL publish no lifter classification tables (only qualifying totals for specific meets), so neither is used.

rank_months.note: model months to reach each rank (index 0-20) at the anchor bodyweight, bars as shown in lb, 3rd-fastest of bench / squat / deadlift / OHP; a smooth estimate, not a promise.

changelog.change: Ladder v1 live (evolution1): Knuckle-Dragger, Primate, Neanderthal, Silverback, Prime, Kong, Apex; flat bodyweight multiples; Prime = Strength Level Intermediate ratios at 175 lb.
swap1 proposal: Prime and Silverback swap places (Prime below Silverback); upper stages from OpenPowerlifting percentiles; v1 awards migrate by threshold. Superseded by swap2.

swap2 proposal: allometric bodyweight scaling (exponent 0.67; men anchored at 180 lb, women at 145 lb); upper tiers from bench anchors and OpenPowerlifting; then every stage entry aligned to a published standard (USPA Classic Raw, FPR classic bench, Strength Level, Symmetric Strength, ExRx).
Hidden five-plate badges (495 lb / 220 kg; bench, squat, deadlift; overhead press stays at two plates) shipped to ladder v1 ahead of the ladder change.

Promoted (Mr Dude via CoS) with two changes: (1) Prime = Strength Level Intermediate on every barbell lift (men at 180 lb: bench 220, squat 298, deadlift 348, OHP 140; a 225 bench at 180 lb qualifies; a v1 Prime stays Prime); (2) Knuckle-Dragger, Primate and Neanderthal lowered to the progression model at weeks -4, 24 and 48 (men bench 65 / 115 / 145 lb), so year 1 gives a new rank about every 1-3 months. Silverback, Kong and Apex keep the aligned swap2 bars.

v1 -> v2 award migration gets a 3% tolerance (migration.tolerance = 0.03): the floor is the highest v2 rank whose five core bars are each <= the v1 bars x k x 1.03. Migration only; computed ranks are unchanged. A woman's v1 Prime at 145 lb now stays Prime.

labels.source_note (shown in the ladder footer) no longer names any stage that is hidden until reached: upper stages are described as following published powerlifting standards. Label only; no threshold or logic change.

Strength Level percentile ladder (Mr Dude via CoS; replaces the plate-friendly anchor proposal and the published-bar alignment): stage bars = Strength Level percentiles at the lifter's bodyweight (Primate beats 10% and Kong top 10%, both interpolated estimates; Neanderthal Novice, Prime Intermediate, Silverback Advanced, Apex Elite; ceiling 99th percentile, extrapolated); SL's per-bodyweight rows replace the allometric 0.67 curve (scaling block retired); bodyweights beyond SL's rows filled from OpenPowerlifting and SL trends (flagged); every bar shown rounds to 5 lb / 2.5 kg with a monotonic guard and ranking compares against it; new "stronger than" percentile line from the same curve. Unchanged: 3 of 5 core lifts with row / dip stand-ins, best-ever e1RM, never demote, 3% migration tolerance (table recomputed), Lean Prime, plate badges.

v1 -> v2 award migration (fix 1, approved): a stored v1 award is judged with the promotion rule (3 of 5 core slots, row / dip stand-ins, 3% tolerance) instead of all 5, plus a stage-name guard (never a lower stage than the v1 award's stage name; floor at tier 1 of that stage). Migration only; computed ranks, percentiles and the curve are unchanged.

Fixes 2 and 3 (Mr Dude via CoS): Primate = beats 8% (top 92%; Beginner + 3/15 x (Novice - Beginner)); Apex = beats 97% (top 3%; Elite + 2/15 x (Elite - Advanced), extrapolated estimate); Kong unchanged (90%); ceiling unchanged (99%, Elite + 4/15 x (Elite - Advanced)). Percentile line follows the new cutoffs; at or above the Apex bar it reads "Top 3% of lifters your size". Migration fix 1, rounding and the monotonic guard unchanged.

v1 -> v2 award migration, option B plus a previous-floor guard (CoS approved; the app has not launched, so no real saved ranks): floor = max(3-of-5 result, the same step number, the previous all-5 floor); a migration alone never unlocks Kong or Apex (capped at Alpha Silverback, or Alpha Kong for Apex, unless the 3-of-5 result reaches that stage). Replaces the stage-name guard. Migration only; curve, percentiles and pacing unchanged.

curve.method: Each stage bar is a Strength Level (SL) population percentile at the lifter's bodyweight. SL's tiers beat 5 / 20 / 50 / 80 / 95% of its lifters (Beginner / Novice / Intermediate / Advanced / Elite). Stage entries: Knuckle-Dragger = the floor (start); Primate = beats 8% (top 92%; estimate: interpolated between Beginner and Novice); Neanderthal = Novice (20%); Prime = Intermediate (50%); Silverback = Advanced (80%); Kong = top 10% (estimate: interpolated between Advanced and Elite); Apex = beats 97% (top 3%; estimate: extrapolated above SL Elite). The Apex ceiling (Alpha Apex sits 2/3 of the way to it) = the 99th percentile, extrapolated (estimate). Chief and Alpha ranks sit at 1/3 and 2/3 of each stage gap.
curve.interpolation: Percentile axis: linear between the tier points (5, 20, 50, 80, 95), i.e. value(p) = T_k + (p - p_k) / (p_(k+1) - p_k) x (T_(k+1) - T_k). Primate (8) = Beginner + 3/15 x (Novice - Beginner); Kong (90) = Advanced + 2/3 x (Elite - Advanced). Above 95 the Advanced -> Elite slope continues: Apex (97) = Elite + 2/15 x (Elite - Advanced); ceiling (99) = Elite + 4/15 x (Elite - Advanced), so the ceiling always sits above Apex. Chosen because SL publishes only the five tier points and linear is the simplest rule that hits every published point exactly; it is an estimate between them.

estimates.primate: beats 8% (top 92%): interpolated between SL Beginner (5%) and Novice (20%): Beginner + 3/15 x (Novice - Beginner)
estimates.kong: top 10%: interpolated between SL Advanced (80%) and Elite (95%)
estimates.apex: beats 97% (top 3%): SL publishes nothing above Elite (95%); the Advanced -> Elite slope is extended: Elite + 2/15 x (Elite - Advanced)
estimates.ceiling: 99th percentile: SL publishes nothing above Elite; the Advanced -> Elite slope is extended (cross-check: men at 180 lb, bench ceiling 355.5 lb is below Symmetric Strength "Elite" 380 lb)

curve.bodyweight: Bars follow SL's per-bodyweight rows directly (10 lb steps), linear between the two rows around the lifter's bodyweight (in lb; kg bodyweights x 2.20462). This replaces the allometric 0.67 curve. Each lift and sex uses its own SL rows, so the bodyweight effect is SL's own (e.g. men's Intermediate bench 1.36x at 130 lb, 1.22x at 180 lb, 1.14x at 300 lb).
curve.clamp: Rows run beyond SL's range to physical bounds (men 100-400 lb, women 80-330 lb), using filled rows (gap_fill). Outside the bounds: below the low bound a load lift keeps the low-bound row's multiple (tier x BW / bound) and a rep lift keeps its reps; above the high bound the high-bound row is held (same loads and reps). So a lighter lifter is never asked for a higher multiple than at the bound, and a heavier lifter is never asked for more load.

gap_fill.rule: Where SL has no row (men below 110 lb or above 310 lb, women below 90 lb or above 260 lb), rows are filled every 10 lb up to the bounds and flagged in tables.<sex>.<lift>.row_meta (source, estimated: true, method). Barbell lifts: ratio-matched to SL at the overlap: SL's edge row x (BW / edge BW)^b, with b = the OpenPowerlifting bodyweight trend for that lift and sex (weighted log-log slope of the median raw full-power best lift per 10 lb bodyweight bin, fitted over the window next to the edge). OHP and barbell row borrow the bench slope (OpenPowerlifting has no press or row). Pull-ups and dips: no other published rep standard by bodyweight exists, so SL's own trend is extended (linear fit to its 5 rows nearest the edge, per tier), floored at 1 rep where SL's edge row is >= 1 (else 0). SL publishes every lift for both sexes, so no lift or sex is missing; the only gaps are bodyweight ranges and the ceiling above Elite.

rounding.formula: bar(unit) = step x floor(raw / step + 0.5 + 1e-4), raw = the curve bar (lb) at the bodyweight, converted to the display unit (settings.unit; kg = lb / 2.20462). Nearest step; an exact half rounds up (the 1e-4 slack absorbs float noise). JS: step * Math.floor(raw / step + 0.5 + 1e-4).
rounding.applies_to: every barbell-load bar (bench, squat, deadlift, OHP and the barbell-row stand-in), at every rank and every bodyweight. Rep bars (pull-ups, dips) are whole reps: ceil(raw - 1e-9).
rounding.guard: monotonic guard, per lift, sex table, unit and bodyweight: walk the 21 rank bars and the ceiling in order; a rounded load bar <= the one before it is raised to the one before + one step, so load bars strictly increase (the guard only ever raises). Rep bars never fall below the bar before; they may be equal where Strength Level publishes "< 1" rep (stored as 0), e.g. the women's pull-up bars below Prime.
rounding.ranking: Ranking compares against the bars as shown in the lifter's own display unit: a set meets a rank when its estimated 1RM in the display unit (or its strict reps) >= that rank's bar at the set's day bodyweight (1e-6 slack). A lifter who hits the number shown always gets the rank. lb and kg bars can differ by rounding, so switching units can move a boundary by up to one step.
rounding.position: ladder position of a set: i + clamp((x - bar_i) / (bar_(i+1) - bar_i), 0, 1) with i = the highest rank whose bar the set meets (bar_21 = the ceiling; at or above it the position is 21); below the first bar: (x - bar_0) / (bar_1 - bar_0) (< 0, still Knuckle-Dragger). A lift's best-ever set = the highest position (ties: the higher value, then the earlier set). Lift rank = min(20, max(0, floor(position))); per-lift progress at shown rank s = clamp(position - s, 0, 1).
rounding.why: Bars on screen are loadable round numbers (5 lb / 2.5 kg), and the number shown is exactly what earns the rank.

percentile.rule: Per lift: from the lift's best ladder position on the same curve as the bars: positions 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 (Primate ... Apex entries) read 8, 20, 50, 80, 90, 97%, the ceiling (21) 99%, linear in between (the Chief and Alpha thirds and SL's linear tiers make this the SL percentile of the shown bars). Below Primate: from SL's Beginner (5%) and Novice (20%) lines at the set's bodyweight, capped at 7.9% (just under Primate); below Beginner: band under_5 (no number). Top rule: at or above the Apex bar (position >= 18) the band is top, shown as "top 3%" (labels.percentile_line_top with {top} = 100 - curve.stage_pct.apex = 3); pct still records the curve value (97-99) for analytics.
percentile.overall: overall = the slot at the 3rd-highest position among the 5 slots after substitution (the promotion rule); fewer than 3 rated slots -> none. Exactly at the Prime bars reads 50%.

card.rule: Card line: band estimate -> labels.percentile_line with {pct} = floor(percent); band top -> labels.percentile_line_top with {top} = 100 - curve.stage_pct.apex; under_5 or no overall -> no line. Per-lift values in report().percentile.lifts.
card.style: small, muted line under the rank

percentile.note: An estimate relative to Strength Level's own user base (self-logged lifts), not peer-reviewed; a model, not a measurement. Follows the computed rank (a held award does not change it).
